html:
The surrender of Japan ended the Second World War. Emperor Hirohito announced Japan's acceptance of Allied terms by radio on 15 August 1945. The formal signing took place on 2 September aboard the American battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay.

Japan gave up after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and the Soviet invasion of Manchuria. The terms were those of the Potsdam declaration of July. The Emperor stayed on the throne, a point Japan's leaders had pressed.

The signing was short. Foreign minister Mamoru Shigemitsu and General Yoshijiro Umezu signed for Japan. General Douglas MacArthur signed for the Allies as Supreme Commander, and Admiral Chester Nimitz for the United States, with delegates of eight other Allied powers.

An American-led occupation followed until 1952. It disbanded the armed forces, wrote a new constitution that renounced war, and brought land reform. News travelled slowly to some island garrisons, and a few soldiers held out for decades. The best known is Hiroo Onoda, who gave up on Lubang island in the Philippines only in 1974. This ended World War II.
